events.description: Two players engage in mutual physical combat on the ice: a player in a white jersey (number 8, 'GRABO') and a player in a red jersey grapple, push, and appear to exchange punches or strikes while locked together.
A second instance of mutual physical combat occurs: the same two players (white #8 and red jersey) are again engaged in close-quarters grappling and striking on the ice.
Two individuals on the ice engage in close physical contact, with one appearing to grab or strike the other; their postures suggest mutual combat rather than a hug or celebration.
Two ice hockey players engage in a physical fight on the ice, grappling and exchanging blows while a referee intervenes.
Two individuals in white jerseys engage in mutual physical combat: one throws a right-handed punch that connects, followed by grappling and clinching with repeated strikes and defensive maneuvers.
Two individuals in hockey practice jerseys engage in a mutual physical fight on the ice, exchanging punches and grappling from frame f0 through f13.

After the mutual fight ends, one individual (in black pants) continues to strike the other (now on hands/knees, wearing red/black socks), who is clearly incapacitated and unable to defend himself — constituting abuse of a helpless victim.

A player in a red jersey is seen confronting a referee; the player's posture and proximity suggest an aggressive physical interaction, possibly grabbing or shoving, as the referee stands close and appears to be restraining or reacting to contact.

The player in the red jersey is being physically guided or pushed by another individual (likely a teammate or official) toward the penalty box or exit, with visible force applied to his upper back/shoulders while he appears subdued or unresisting—consistent with post-conflict removal of a disruptive individual.
A large group of ice hockey players from two teams engage in a multi-person brawl near the boards, with pushing, shoving, and grappling visible across multiple frames.
After the initial scrum disperses, two players (one in white/green, one in black/red) continue to fight on the ice, with a referee intervening; the combat includes clinching and attempted takedowns.
A player in a white jersey (number 30) delivers repeated punches to an opponent who is already down on the ice and appears unable to defend himself, constituting abuse of a helpless victim.
